# HChipGroup

> An array-valued filter group or removable set of selected tags.

[Start with the Hearth UI agent index](../../../llms.txt). This describes repository source for version 0.4.0. Match documentation to your installed source/release.

## Identity

- Vue export: `HChipGroup` from `@hearth-ui/vue`.
- Custom element: `<hearth-chip-group>`.
- Constructor: `HearthChipGroupElement` from `@hearth-ui/elements`.
- Category: Controls.
- [Implementation](https://github.com/samishal1998/hearth-ui/blob/main/src/components/HChipGroup.vue).

## Choose and use it correctly

- The model is an array of selected values. Default mode shows all options as toggles; removable mode shows only selected options with remove actions.
- This is filter/application state, not a form-associated field. Use HMultiSelect when repeated form submission values are needed.

## Public API

options: SelectOption[] · modelValue: string[] · label: string · removable, disabled: boolean

A `?` marks optional source props. Props with defaults may be omitted. Internal `formDisabled` and `control-sync` plumbing is excluded below; do not use it in application code.

```ts
type Props = {
    options: SelectOption[];
    modelValue?: string[];
    label?: string;
    removable?: boolean;
    disabled?: boolean;
};
```

### Defaults

```ts
{ options: () => [], modelValue: () => [], label: "Filters" }
```

### Events

update:modelValue(values), change(values), remove(value)

```ts
type Emits = {
    "update:modelValue": [
        values: string[]
    ];
    change: [
        values: string[]
    ];
    remove: [
        value: string
    ];
};
```

Vue-emitted custom-element events expose argument arrays in `event.detail`. Listen on the element. Native events such as `click` retain their normal payloads. The elements package provides framework-independent DOM event types.

### Slots

default

Vue uses `<template #slotName>`; custom elements use `<div slot="slotName">`. Web components do not support Vue scoped slots.

### CSS parts

base

Use `hearth-chip-group::part(part-name)` for an exposed part or inherited `--h-*` tokens for shared styling. Native Vue components use the shared stylesheet and `h-*` classes.

## Supporting types

```ts
export interface SelectOption {
    value: string;
    label: string;
    disabled?: boolean;
}
```

## Vue example

```vue
<script setup lang="ts">
import { ref } from 'vue';
import { HChipGroup } from '@hearth-ui/vue';
import '@hearth-ui/vue/styles.css';
const filters = ref<string[]>(['media']);
const options = [{value:'media',label:'Media'},{value:'home',label:'Home'}];
</script>

<template>
  <HChipGroup v-model="filters" label="Application filters" :options="options" />
</template>
```

## Web-component example

Provide a mount point. For field submission, use an owning native form; the auth page already contains its own form.

```html
<div id="example"></div>
```

This is bundler-based ESM. For raw HTML, load `dist/themes.css` with a link and import `registerElements` from `./dist/elements/index.js` instead. Initial array/object properties are assigned before connection to establish reset defaults.

```js
import { registerElements } from '@hearth-ui/elements';
import '@hearth-ui/elements/themes.css';
registerElements();

const mount = document.querySelector('#example');
const element = document.createElement('hearth-chip-group');
Object.assign(element, {
  "label": "Application filters",
  "modelValue": [
    "media"
  ],
  "options": [
    {
      "value": "media",
      "label": "Media"
    },
    {
      "value": "home",
      "label": "Home"
    }
  ]
});

element.addEventListener('change', event => {
  const [value] = event.detail;
  // Update your application state using value.
});

mount.append(element);
```
